Prerequisites

In this game, we pair each number with the name of its family, using the second column of Table 1 of the text Naming. To make the most of this activity, we recommend reviewing first:

  • Naming: in this text, Table 1 presents the names of the families, from Quintillion down to Units and from Tenths down to Trillionths ().
  • Sequence game (Orders): the game whose mechanics this one follows, pairing numbers with the names of their orders ().

Rules

The goal of the game is to pair each number with the name of its family, following the second column of Table 1 of Naming: Quintillion, Quadrillion, Trillion, Billion, Million, Thousand, Units, Tenths, Hundredths, Thousandths, Millionths, Billionths and Trillionths. In each round, six numbers appear on the left, each one belonging to a different family, and the names of these same six families appear on the right in a different order. Select a number and then select the name of its family; if the pair is correct, both buttons are highlighted and stay in place.

The game has three levels. In the first level, six numbers are drawn at random from the seven families greater than zero, from Quintillion down to Units. In the second level, three of the drawn numbers are greater than zero and three are smaller than zero, mixing families like Million with families like Hundredths. In the third level, all six numbers are smaller than zero, drawn at random among the families of Tenths, Hundredths, Thousandths, Millionths, Billionths and Trillionths.

When you match all six pairs of a level, a congratulations message is displayed and the button Next level becomes available. After finishing the third level, a final congratulations message is displayed. You can start a new round at any time by clicking the button New Game.

Sequence game (Families)

Connect each number on the left with the name of its family on the right. Select a number, then select its name to form the pair. Before choosing the family, ask yourself whether the number is greater than or smaller than zero: the families greater than zero take whole numbers, while those smaller than zero take decimals closer to zero.

PERFECT! You matched all the numbers with the names of their families!
